{{Short description|Danish mycologist}}
{{Use British English|date=June 2021}}
'''Anders Munk''' (1922 in [[Kolding]] – June 1989 in [[Copenhagen]]) was a Danish [[mycologist]]. He was an expert of the fungal group colloquially known as the [[Pyrenomycetes]],<ref name="Truszkowska 1992"/> and best known for his 1957 work "Danish Pyrenomycetes".<ref name="Myconews 1990"/>

==Biography==
Munk's introduction to mycology was from [[Poul Larsen]], who was previously a teacher and a former colleague of Munk's parents. Around that time Munk also made contact with biologist [[Øjvind Winge]], who introduced Munk to the Pyrenomycetes, which were also his own main interest. Munk started studying [[botany]] at the [[University of Copenhagen]] in 1940. His interest in the fungi was further enhanced after reading [[John Axel Nannfeldt]]'s 1932 work on the [[morphology (biology)|morphology]] and [[systematics]] of the [[discomycetes]]. Munk worked for some summers at the then-newly started {{ill|Mols Laboratory of Natural History|da|Molslaboratoriet}}, where he increased his knowledge about the ecology of the Pyrenomycetes.<ref name="Læssøe 1990"/>

After graduating in 1946, Munk got a short-term job at Løvens Kemiske Fabrik (now [[LEO Pharma]]). He did not enjoy the work (manufacturing [[antibiotic]]s), and shortly after started teaching at {{ill|Th.Langs Skoler|da}}, a private school in [[Silkeborg]]. He continued his graduate studies in his spare time, and defended his doctoral [[dissertation]] in 1953. Apart from a short-term scholarship with [[Morten Lange]] in 1963, the rest of Munk's career was largely devoted to teaching.<ref name="Læssøe 1990"/>

Munk was married to Ruth, who he met as a fellow student at university, and with whom he had four children. He spent the last years of his life in pain from [[spondylosis]] of the [[cervical vertebrae]].<ref name="Læssøe 1990"/>

==Eponymy==
Several [[fungi]] have been [[eponym|named to honour]] Munk, including: ''[[Capronia munkii]]'' {{small|Unter. (1995)}};<ref name="Untereiner 1995"/> ''[[Endoxyla munkii]]'' {{small|Unter. 1993)}};<ref name="Untereiner 1993"/> ''[[Hypoxylon munkii]]'' {{small|Whalley, Hammelev & Talig. (1988)}};<ref name="Whalley et al. 1988"/> and ''[[Trichodelitschia munkii]]'' {{small|N.Lundq. (1964)}}.<ref name="Lundqvist 1964"/>
